report.summary: Analyzed chunk 2 of drafts.py: two public functions, set_status and apply_payload, with docstring claims about status transitions, idempotency, and no filesystem writes.
risks: set_status line 121 | medium | Function writes to filesystem despite docstring claim of no filesystem touch for 'applied' status. | Check if the docstring is misleading or if 'applied' status is special-cased elsewhere.
apply_payload line 145 | low | Call to set_status may raise ValueError if status is invalid, but set_status is called with 'applied' which is valid. | Ensure 'applied' is always in _STATUSES.

handoff.purpose: Defines set_status and apply_payload functions for draft lifecycle management.

symbols.name: set_status
symbols.note: Updates draft JSON file with new status and timestamp.

symbols.name: apply_payload
symbols.note: Calls set_status which writes to filesystem, then returns packet dict.

claims.text: Transition a draft's lifecycle. Returns the updated draft, or None if the id is unknown; raises ValueError on an invalid status.
claims.why: Code checks status against _STATUSES and raises ValueError; returns None if p is None or not file; returns updated draft dict.

claims.text: This does NOT touch the filesystem of the target repo -- 'applied' only marks the proposal as handled
claims.why: The function writes to the draft file via p.write_text(), which is a filesystem write (though not to the target repo, but to the drafts directory). The claim says 'does NOT touch the filesystem' but it does.
Calling set_status multiple times with same draft_id and status will overwrite the file with same content, no side effects beyond the write.

claims.text: The review packet a human / the Claude lane needs to ACTUALLY apply a draft: the objective, the target paths, and the proposal text. Marks the draft 'applied' (handled) but performs no write itself -- returning the packet IS the handoff.
claims.why: The function calls set_status which writes to the filesystem. So it does perform a write, contradicting 'performs no write itself'.

claims.text: None if the id is unknown.
claims.why: If get_draft returns None, the function returns None.

observations.what: set_status writes to the draft file, contradicting the docstring claim that it does not touch filesystem.
apply_payload calls set_status which writes, contradicting the claim that it performs no write itself.
The docstring of set_status mentions 'applied' only marks the proposal as handled, but the function does not differentiate statuses; it writes for any status.
No validation that draft_id is non-empty string; _safe_path may return None for invalid inputs.
